rv.q: It’s an hour and a half of comedy heaven, and I’d gladly watch it annually.
Nobody is too holy to avoid the occasional easy target, including the Chicago Cubs and the old joke about Adam and Steve.
I found myself a little stumped by what had now become an edgy brief for atheism.
The show is intermittently funny, but it's also repetitive and one-note, with limited comic range despite the rich satirical possibilities of its premise.
I'd rather go straight to hell than sit through 'An Act of God' again.
I thoroughly enjoyed David Javerbaum's theological satire last summer when it starred Jim Parsons, and I could watch Hayes's bratty-campy shtick all night.
Hayes carries the whole 90 minutes lightly on his narrow shoulders, glibly rewriting the commandments and pointing out all the absurd mistakes humanity's made interpreting the old ones.
The play by David Javerbaum has laugh-management issues.
We long for something more, and we won't find it in An Act of God.
Neither heavenly nor hellish, “An Act of God” is primarily for fans of Jim Parsons.
For a play lampooning the deity revered by half the earth's population, An Act of God is surprisingly risk-averse.
Even at just 90 minutes, “An Act of God” (directed by the prolific Joe Mantello) is long-winded and full of unoriginal jabs at easy targets, but it is cute and occasionally witty.
Overall the play is laugh out loud funny; Parsons is brilliant in his role
